cues: As he grew, his reading leaned to astronomy and chemistry.

His school's Walker Library was excellent in history but weak in science, so a teacher wrote him a testimonial that got him into the Science Museum library, where he devoured huge chemistry treatises.
At Oxford he had the Radcliffe Science Library and the Bodleian, which goes back to sixteen oh two.
There he stumbled on Theodore Hook, a forgotten nineteenth century wit said to have improvised more than five hundred operas, and decided to write his life.
The lesson: one library cannot hold everything; a hungry reader goes looking.
